title: AI literacy in K-12: a systematic literature review
abstract: Systematic review of how AI literacy is being introduced in K-12. The authors analyze published interventions and frameworks and find that learners can develop AI literacy across conceptual, practical, and ethical dimensions, but that AI is rarely integrated as a structured part of the curriculum and that teacher preparation and assessment remain weak points.

title: Developing Middle School Students' AI Literacy
abstract: Reports the design and classroom implementation of a middle-school AI literacy curriculum. Following the curriculum, students were able to train and evaluate simple machine learning models, explain how training data shapes a model's behavior, and discuss the societal and ethical implications of AI systems they use.

title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) literacy in early childhood education: The challenges and opportunities
abstract: Reviews opportunities and challenges of introducing AI literacy in early childhood education. Argues that young children can grasp age-appropriate AI concepts when teaching is concrete, playful, and embedded in familiar everyday contexts, while cautioning about developmental fit, teacher readiness, and the need for ethics-aware design.

title: A is for Artificial Intelligence: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence Activities on Young Children's Perceptions of Robots
abstract: Empirical study of AI learning activities with young children. Hands-on activities measurably changed children's perceptions of intelligent agents, improving their ability to reason about what such systems can and cannot do and reducing naive anthropomorphic assumptions about robots and AI.

title: Family as a Third Space for AI Literacies: How do children and parents learn about AI together?
abstract: Study of children and parents learning about AI together at home. Through guided, social exploration of everyday smart devices, children developed algorithmic awareness - recognizing that such devices make data-driven decisions - and learned to question the behavior of the AI embedded in everyday tools.

title: What Is the Impact of ChatGPT on Education? A Rapid Review of the Literature
abstract: Rapid review of early literature on ChatGPT in education. Finds clear potential to support teaching and learning alongside recurring concerns about inaccurate or fabricated output, over-reliance, and academic integrity, and stresses that learners need to verify AI-generated content against reliable sources.
